Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

menu — the list of dishes in a restaurant. Example: The waiter brings the menu.
order — to ask for food in a restaurant. Example: Are you ready to order?
waiter — a person who serves food. Example: The waiter brings the bill.
dish — food prepared in a particular way. Example: My favourite dish is spicy chicken.
drink — liquid you take in, or to take liquid in. Example: What would you like to drink?
dessert — sweet food at the end of a meal. Example: The dessert is apple pie.
bill — the paper showing what you must pay. Example: Could we have the bill, please?
water — the clear liquid we drink. Example: A glass of water, please.
coffee — a hot brown drink made from beans. Example: I drink coffee in the morning.
please — a polite word when asking. Example: A coffee, please.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What would you like?
• I'd like the fish, please.
• Nothing for me, thank you.
• Could we have the bill?
• Here is the menu.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
The waiter brings the menu. I would like the soup and the fish. My friend orders a dessert and a coffee. We ask for the bill after the meal.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: What would you like to drink? B: Water, please. A: And for dessert? B: Nothing, thank you. Could we have the bill?
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Roleplay ordering a meal in a café.
